description.para: Defines constants for supported and unsupported reset actions.

parameterdescription.para: Indicates whether reset status check is supported.
Indicates whether pulse reset action is supported.
Indicates whether reset assert and deassert are supported.

simplesect.para:
Bit fields decide the supported actions as follows: BIT 1 is assert/deassert, BIT 2 is pulse, and BIT 3 is reset status. A set bit indicates that the corresponding action is supported, and vice versa.
C-style signature: u8 XRESETPS_SUPPORTED_ACT(u8 ResetSupport, u8 PulseSupport, u8 AssertSupport)

briefdescription.para: Checks whether assert/deassert reset is supported.

simplesect.para: 1 if supported, or 0 if not supported.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether pulse reset is supported.

simplesect.para: 1 if supported, or 0 if not supported.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether reset status check is supported.

simplesect.para: 1 if supported, or 0 if not supported.

parameterdescription.para: Address of the register to read.
Address of the register to write.
32-bit value to write to the register.

simplesect.para: C-style signature: void XResetPs_WriteReg(u32 RegAddress, u32 Data)

briefdescription.para: No delay, no power state check.
Defines the type of pulse reset to execute for peripherals.

detaileddescription.para:
Three types of pulse reset are possible:
Pulse with no delay and no power state validation.
Pulse with delay but no power state validation.
Pulse with delay and power state validation.

briefdescription.para: Defines reset actions on the peripherals.
Defines reset IDs of peripherals mapped to PMUFW reset IDs.

detaileddescription.para: These reset IDs are not offset by 1000 and are relative.

briefdescription.para: Defines possible values for reset status of peripherals.
Looks up the device configuration by unique device ID or base address.

detaileddescription.para: XResetPs_ConfigTable[] contains the configuration information for each device in the system.

simplesect.para: A pointer to the configuration found, or NULL if the specified device ID or base address is not found. See xresetps.h for the definition of XResetPs_Config.
In the XSCT/classic flow, the function uses DeviceId to look up the device configuration.

briefdescription.para: Initializes a specific reset controller instance or driver.

detaileddescription.para: This function must be called before other functions of the driver are called.

briefdescription.para: Asserts reset for a specific peripheral based on reset ID.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if reset assertion is successful.

briefdescription.para: Deasserts reset for a specific peripheral based on reset ID.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if reset deassertion is successful.

briefdescription.para: Pulse resets a specific peripheral based on reset ID.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if pulse reset is successful.

briefdescription.para: Gets the reset status for a specific peripheral based on reset ID.

parameterdescription.para: Status of the reset for ResetID: 1 if asserted and 0 if released.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the status is fetched successfully.
